args.summary: checkout-api became unhealthy after deploy of v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18% and failing health checks. Remediation performed: rolled back all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release previously healthy in production. Rollback completed and verified: all regions now on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate down to 0.2%. Follow-up: root-cause the v2.3.1 failure and stage v2.3.1-rc appropriately before re-attempting a deploy.
args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy; rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed** the issue: checkout-api was running v2.3.1 across all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate and failing health checks. The deployment history showed v2.3.1 as unhealthy in production; the most recent healthy production release was **v2.3.0**.
2. **Rolled back** checkout-api to v2.3.0 in all production regions. The rollout completed and verified successfully.
3. **Confirmed recovery**: checkout-api is now healthy on v2.3.0 with error rate down to 0.2%.
4. **Opened a SEV2 incident** (INC-0001, on-call paged) documenting the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, current healthy status, and follow-up items (root-cause v2.3.1, fix the rc pipeline before re-deploying).

Note: no change-manager approval was needed since v2.3.0 had previously been healthy in production — this was a rollback to a known-good release.
